audit_notes: Model: steady near-wall transport of diatom cells with a first-order wall reaction whose effective attachment velocity is time-averaged over service and idle: k_eff = k_c*a*[f_idle + (1-f_idle)*exp(-tau_w/tau_adh)]. Retained settlement flux J = k_eff*c_b/(1+Da), Da = delta*k_eff/D. Design (a = 0.5, tau_adh = 15 Pa, f_idle = 0.25): k_eff = 1e-4*0.5*(0.25+0.75*0.189) = 1.96e-5 m/s, Da = 0.098, J = 1.78e4 1/(m^2 s). Baseline silicone foul-release (a = 1, tau_adh = 30 Pa): k_eff = 1e-4*(0.25+0.75*0.435) = 5.76e-5 m/s, Da = 0.288, J = 4.47e4 1/(m^2 s). Expected gain about 60 % lower retained settlement flux, somewhat less than the parent's 67 % because idle periods are now included; the idle share is where the steric sticking reduction matters. Caveats: sticking probability 0.5 and adhesion strength 15 Pa are fresh-surface lab values and fully drive the gain; ageing, conditioning films and oil are not modelled; settlement flux is a proxy for slime thickness. Parameter check: all positive and in range; u_tau = 0.156 m/s at 25 Pa. Dimensionless: Damkoehler 0.098 (design) and 0.288 (baseline), reaction-limited regime; shear-to-adhesion ratio 1.67 (design) vs 0.83 (baseline). No structural load. Simulation coefficient: design effective attachment velocity 1.96e-5 m/s (informational).
